subject: design-technology

moments.title: Bakelite patented
moments.body: Baekeland creates the first fully synthetic plastic, marketed as 'the material of a thousand uses'.
moments.takeaway: Modern materials enabled product categories that had not existed.

moments.title: Nylon
moments.body: Carothers's team at DuPont synthesises nylon, which goes commercial in 1939.
moments.takeaway: Industrial chemistry created textiles from coal and air.

moments.title: Kevlar
moments.body: Kwolek's para-aramid fibre is five times stronger than steel by weight. It transforms protective clothing.
moments.takeaway: Single chemists can change what is possible to wear.

now.title: Plastics today
now.body: Microplastics are now a global pollution issue. Bioplastics and chemical recycling are active research areas.
now.open_questions: What does the next generation of materials look like?

reflection: Synthetic materials make modern products possible and modern pollution unavoidable.
